messages.subject: oSCR sex ratio??
messages.body_plain:
I'm wondering if anyone knows a way to work out sex ratio? I'm not sure if psi(male) in oSCR works the same as the Bayesian format. If you look in Elliot and Gopalswamy (2017) table 1, there is a formula for converting psi(sex) to sex ratio: 1-psi(sex)/psi(sex). Just wondering if anyone knows if it is the same formula or is there a different method or way to implement it in oSCR?

Many thanks in advance,

Rachael

Sex ratio=1−ψsexψ

messages.subject: State space using GIS
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I was wondering if it is possible to create the state space in a multi-session study using this formula (for externally GIS)

df <-data.frame(X=X,Y=Y)
ss <-list(df)

I tried it in a single-session study and it worked, but every time I try to use it in a multi-session study an error appears saying that I need to create a state space for EACH session. I can't find any examples of multi-session studies using this formula so I don't know how to create one per session.

I already created the state space in the multi-session study using this other formula: ss <-make.ssDF(scrFrame, buffer, res). But I wanted to know if it's possible with the first formula.

In case to be possible, can you show me an example for a three session study? all of the session uses the same coordinates (X,Y)

Thank you so much!

messages.subject: RE: [oscr] State space using GIS
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

As long as you are fine using the same state space for both sessions, then the following should work:

df <-data.frame(X=X,Y=Y)

ss <-list(df, df)

If you want different ones for each sessions then something like this can be used:

df1 <-data.frame(X=X1,Y=Y1)

df2 <-data.frame(X=X2,Y=Y2)

ss <-list(df1, df2)

Hope that helps 😊

Chris

messages.subject: oSCR design
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm planning to deploy some camera traps to monitor Hartmann's mountain zebra, and came across this great tool for optimization. However, I'm having some issues on the process, and I think this is the right place to get a solution.

- My first issue is when I'm defining beta0, I'm not sure how to get this parameter. I'm using parameters from a previous study where: p0 = 0.04, and I set K = 60 days, so according to the vignette, beta0 = log(p0*K). But then, you have temp = exp(beta0), and again p0 = to temp/K, here is where I got confused and asked myself, what is actually p0? I know that that's the baseline encounter probability, but why we have to recalculate again here, if I got it already?

- When creating the testdesign using the function scrdesignGA(), I get a warning message saying: In optimaltraps$fixed <- c(rep("no",  lenght(des$bestsol)), rep("yes", : Coercing LHS to a list)). This is what I think leads to the error I get later when trying to plot the testdesign object.

- When ploting the testdesign object I get the following error message:
Error in xy.coords(x,y) : 'x' is a list, but does not have the components 'x' and 'y'.
It shows up two plots, one showing the lines of Pop average and Pop best, and other with the state-space without the expected camera deployment. Therefore, I went back saved the alltraps object as csv, loaded into R. That worked only producing the same two plots, but this time with the cameras deployed, missing the histogram.

- Lastly, I went on trying simulations, and I got an error:
[1] "Simulation Number 1"
Size of state-space: 550 pixels
Try 1
Error in x[, 1], -y[i, 1] : non-numeric argument to binary operator.
Here I don't know what does it means.

Thank you in Advance

messages.subject: Issues with oSCR.fit
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I’m a PhD student and I’m working on a two years CMR data (collected from my PhD project) of a subterranean population of Strinati’s cave salamander. We performed the study inside a cave, equipped with a 1m square grid of 5x42 plots, where we captured and photographed the ventral patterns of individuals, noting sex (M, F and SA – subadults) and capture site. This protocol was done about once a month in the last two years (i.e., 1 session and 30 occasions). I added some of the trap covariates that we registered (i.e., surface temperature of cave wall during the peak activity and distance from the entrance).

I followed the RBS worked example for preparing and analyzing the data. I was able to create the data2oscr object and the state space object. However, I have troubles when I try to run models,  for example with the base model (m1) it says "Error in nlm(msLL.sex, scrFrame = scrFrame, p = pv, pn = pn, D = D, nG = nG,  : non-finite value supplied by 'nlm'.", while if I try to add trap covariates (m2) I receive the message “Error in dm.trap[[s]][[k]] %*% c(t.beta[s, ]) : non-conformable arguments”.

I’m wondering if there is an underlying problem with data setting, because I repeated multiple times data formatting and analysis and I believe those are correct. Attached the R code and scrFrame plot.

I would appreciate any advice, thank you in advance!

Giacomo Rosa

library(devtools)

library(oSCR)

ss.edf<-read.table("str.edf”,header=1)

ss.tdf<-read.table("str.tdf ",header = 1)

head(ss.edf)

Detector Session ID Sex Occasion

1       B4       1  1  SA        1

2       B5       1  3  SA        1

3       B8       1  4   M        1

4       B9       1  5  SA        1

5      A10       1  6   F        1

6      E10       1  7   M        1

head(ss.tdf)

Detector X Y t.oper sep  Temp Distance

1     A1 1 1      1   / 12.87        1

2     A2 1 2      1   / 12.83        2

3     A3 1 3      1   / 11.97        3

4     A4 1 4      1   / 11.83        4

5     A5 1 5      1   / 11.70        5

6     A6 1 6      1   / 11.73        6

ss.data<-data2oscr(edf=ss.edf,

                    sess.col=2,

                    id.col=3,

                    occ.col=5,

                    trap.col=1,

                    sex.col=4,

                    tdf=list(ss.tdf),

                    K=c(30),

                    ntraps= 210,

                    trapcov.names=c("Temp","Distance"),

                    sex.nacode = "SA",

                    tdf.sep="/")

names(ss.data)

ss.sf<-ss.data$scrFrame

names(ss.sf)

caphist <- ss.sf$caphist

traps <- ss.sf$traps

trapCovs <-ss.sf$trapCovs

indCovs<-ss.sf$indCovs

sf<-make.scrFrame(caphist = caphist, traps = traps, indCovs=indCovs, trapCovs = trapCovs, type = "scr")

plot(sf,jit=2)

ss.ss<-make.ssDF(scrFrame=sf,buffer=3,res=0.5)

str(ss.ss)

plot(ssDF=ss.ss,scrFrame=sf)

m1<-oSCR.fit(model=list(D~1, #density

                        p0~1,#detection

                        sig~1), #spaceuse

             scrFrame=sf,ssDF=ss.ss)

m2<- oSCR.fit(model=list(D~1, #density

                        p0~Temp,#detection

                        sig~1), #spaceuse

             scrFrame=sf,ssDF=ss.ss)

messages.subject: Re: [oscr] Issues with oSCR.fit
messages.body_plain:
hello,
 The error here might be poor starting values for the model parameters.  You should try to ballpark those as best you can and see if that makes a difference.   If you run oSCR.fit with the getStarts = TRUE option then it will tell you what should be the order of the starting values.
regards
andy
